we studied the impact of mild hyperthermia (40°C) as a therapeutic intervention for fatty livers using in‐depth proteomic and lipoprotein profiling of whole organ perfusion and precision‐cut liver slices.
Tissue biopsies and perfusate samples were collected at baseline (0 h, 37°C) and every 1 h of hyperthermic or normothermic (control) perfusion.
PCLS tissue was collected at 0, 3, 24, and 48 h for analysis.
Control samples (37°C) were obtained from livers that met all viability criteria
baseline parameters were taken at 37°C before increasing the temperature to 40°C for another 3 h
PCLS were incubated... at 37°C or 40°C for 3, 24, or 48 h

we performed differential analysis of the identified proteins in all samples over time. This showed that the perfusate exhibited a moderate but continually increasing number of significant (p < 0.05) protein IDs over time when compared to baseline.
